title: Armstrong's repertoire beyond the recorded pop tunes
summary: Besides pop and show tunes, the band played older numbers like Shine and Black and Blue, which Armstrong had recorded before coming back to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: He got to do it. Well, the tunes that the band recorded -- they were all pop tunes or show tunes and things like that.
You know, when you playing gigs, what else was in the library that wasn't recorded? Did he have some of the older tunes that he liked to play sometimes?
Like -- did he do "Dipper Mouth" or --
Yeah, we'd do -- he would do "Shine" and "Black and Blue" -- that's a tune -- that is a song that's really beautiful. Fats Waller 2
Yes, it is. Bill Garland wrote that.
Yeah. You heard him do that didn't you? "I don't know --"
"-- just why I'm so black and blue."
Well, he had recorded things with big bands before he came back to Chicago and he had those arrangements with him, I take it? Did he?
He had recorded "Black and Blue" and Les Hite's band "Shine", for instance, with Wes Hartspon. (Mr. Garland)
And then you had -- did you make new arrangements on those songs that he had recorded before, or did he have some arrangements with him when he came back to Chicago?
